context.purpose: Turn a short plain-text script into a synthetic voiceover draft: a canonical PCM16 mono 22050 Hz WAV from the fixed offline eSpeak NG en-us voice or one explicitly selected voice (en-gb, fr-fr or es), proven by a fresh native re-synthesis of the captured text. Complements audio preparation (SoX), transcription (whisper.cpp) and archiving (FLAC), which cannot create narration. Unsuitable for human-quality voice, other voices, languages, variants or accents, translation, SSML or phoneme control, long scripts, and any claim of intelligibility, pronunciation or accessibility.
context.assumptions: A script of at most 1024 Unicode code points and 8 KiB, a literal string or an absolute local UTF-8 .txt file or artifact, within the documented Unicode profile, with native controls, markup and phoneme escapes refused. A configured eSpeak NG 1.52.0 espeak-ng executable with its matching native data; the host has no speech synthesizer. The finished narration must stay within 120 seconds and 8 MiB.
context.constraints: One operation, narrate. The voice (en-us unless the optional voice selects en-us, en-gb, fr-fr or es), pitch (50), amplitude (100), input encoding (UTF-8, -b1) and output (PCM16 mono 22050 Hz, 44-byte header) are fixed; only rateWpm (integer 120-240, default 175) and the optional voice are authored; an absent voice keeps the original en-us plans and receipts unchanged. Control characters, [[ ]] phoneme escapes, markup, text without a letter or digit, silent output and unsupported runtimes are refused. The narration is synthetic, not a human recording.
context.inspection: Inspect narration.wav (listen to it) and espeakng-summary.json (script bytes, SHA-256, code points and lines, requested voice with its listed name and file, rate, audio geometry and duration, PCM SHA-256, peak and nonzero samples, runtime identity and native-data fingerprint). verify needs the trusted espeak-ng (SCHEMAXIS_ESPEAKNG or a stored espeakng location; --espeakng belongs to run): it re-synthesises the captured text in a private directory and compares every PCM byte; there is no host speech synthesizer. Read the words as well as listening.
context.recovery: INVALID_ESPEAKNG_SOURCE: author exactly one of text and source; source is an absolute regular local .txt file. INVALID_ESPEAKNG_TEXT: remove the named control character, [[ ]] phoneme escape or markup, use UTF-8 and line feeds, and write at least one word. ESPEAKNG_BUDGET: shorten the script below 1024 code points and 8 KiB, or shorten or speed up a narration over 120 s or 8 MiB. ESPEAKNG_SILENT_OUTPUT: write words the selected voice can speak. ESPEAKNG_OUTPUT_REJECTED: the native WAV is not canonical PCM16 mono 22050 Hz; use eSpeak NG 1.52.0. INTERPRETER_NOT_FOUND: configure espeak-ng (--espeakng, SCHEMAXIS_ESPEAKNG or a stored location). UNSUPPORTED_RUNTIME: use eSpeak NG 1.52.0 with its matching native data and the selected voice listed exactly (en-us, en-gb, fr-fr or es): a runtime that lists another voice, or none, is refused rather than allowed to fall back. VERIFICATION_FAILED: the published bytes, retained evidence, JSON types, or the verifying runtime or native data differ; verify with the matching runtime and data or run again into a fresh directory.

workflow.scope: A verified file or text artifact (for example a whisper.cpp transcript.txt) can be the source; the WAV and summary publish through the normal scheduler with provenance. The narration feeds SoX conform and FLAC encodeLossless. A French narration can be conformed with SoX and archived as lossless FLAC (examples/schemaxis/espeakng-voice-archive-workflow.json).

composition.scope: Shared document references, pure expressions and finite studies resolve before the native recipe.

lifecycle.timeout: One total deadline covers the version probe, voice query, native narration and the fresh verification re-synthesis. Each child CPU 60 s, address space 2 GiB, output size capped at 16 MiB (a runaway guard; the 120 s and 8 MiB budgets are judged on the finished file); standalone verify has a 180 s budget.
lifecycle.cancellation: Shared owned process-group cancellation; serial children and a final cancellation/deadline check before publication. A failed run removes its unverified publications.
lifecycle.logs: Authored/effective plan, captured script and byte binding, native WAV, exact launchers, input hashes, stage stdout/stderr/submissions (the version output names a private data directory and stays private) and an independently computed summary.
lifecycle.verification: The captured script is re-checked against the plain-text profile, then the trusted espeak-ng re-synthesises it in a private directory outside the run with the declared rate; every PCM byte, the sample count, rate and channels are compared with the published WAV, and the host rebuilds the canonical WAV with struct and wave. Runtime identity and native-data fingerprint must match the recorded ones. Not a host synthesizer: espeak-ng is the oracle, and a coherent rewrite of the captured text is an unauthenticated trust anchor.

losses: Control characters, phoneme escapes and markup are refused, not removed; the synthesizer may skip or expand characters by its own rules.
The file is captured byte for byte; nothing is normalised and nothing but the words is carried.
data.scope: Captured regular local .txt file or artifact.

traits.voice: eSpeak NG en-us by default, or the explicitly selected en-us, en-gb, fr-fr or es, requested

losses: Synthetic speech: no prosody control, only four voices (en-us default, en-gb, fr-fr, es), no translation or language detection; not a human recording; accent, pronunciation and intelligibility are not certified.
data.scope: One narration.wav of at most 120 seconds and 8 MiB, then a text summary.

inspection.scope: JSON script hashes and counts, requested voice and rate, audio geometry, duration, PCM hash and peaks, runtime identity and data fingerprint.
inspection.limits: Host-authored summary recomputed during verification; no playback and no host speech synthesizer.

authoring.reuse: Change the text, or the absolute source file, or rateWpm. Retain source bytes for provenance; same-path byte changes invalidate scheduler reuse.

workflow.scope: A verified file or text artifact (for example a whisper.cpp transcript.txt) can be the source; narration.wav and the summary publish through the normal scheduler with provenance and feed SoX conform or FLAC.

composition.scope: Shared document references, pure expressions and finite studies resolve before the native recipe.

reusable-inputs.scope: A source file path and its captured byte digest participate in reuse identity; a literal text has no external input.

source-authoring.scope: Editable JSON text or source with common undo and validation.

property-authoring.scope: Common pointer forms expose text, source and rateWpm; the contract has no other authored properties.

conversion.scope: narrate creates a synthetic draft from text; it is not a named format conversion and no automatic conversion is inserted. Use SoX conform and FLAC encodeLossless as explicit downstream steps.

native-inspection.scope: No interactive native inspection; the WAV and its JSON summary are ordinary publications.

mpi.scope: The recipe is serial; each native process is a single thread.

time-batches.scope: No temporal batching; common finite studies remain available.

live-editing.scope: No persistent native session; edit JSON then create a new bounded run.

native-save.scope: WAV and summary publications are supported; there is no application session or project save.

cases.scope: Literal 16-word, 91-character ASCII script at the default 175 words per minute. The code point, byte, line and format expectations are hand-counted from the text, and the duration is the independent words/rate estimate (16 words at 175 wpm = 5.49 s) with a deliberately wide 15 percent tolerance because the synthesizer adds its own pauses; nothing is copied from the observed output. The decision is the fresh native re-synthesis compared byte for byte with the published PCM.

Three-line UTF-8 file (30 words, 169 code points, 173 bytes because four letters carry accents) at 140 words per minute, so the explicit UTF-8 input path and the file source are exercised. Counts are hand-derived from the fixture; the duration estimate is 30 words at 140 wpm = 12.86 s within 15 percent. The decision is the fresh native re-synthesis compared byte for byte.

Literal 16-word script with digits at the 240 words per minute maximum (80 characters). Counts are hand-derived; the duration estimate is 16 words at 240 wpm = 4.0 s within 15 percent (digits expand to spoken words). The decision is the fresh native re-synthesis compared byte for byte.

completion.scope: New adaptor 2026-10-25: schemaxis.espeakng/1 narrate route, plain-text profile, fixed native eSpeak NG 1.52.0 en-us stages, canonical PCM16 WAV reader and writer, fresh trusted native re-synthesis verification, discovery, guidance, Studio starters and bounded native acceptance. Allocation 57 (2026-10-25) adds the optional closed voice choice en-us, en-gb, fr-fr or es with exact per-voice listing checks, per-voice native-data fingerprints and conditional voice bindings; an absent voice keeps the original plans, launchers, summaries and receipts.
